title: Now, Gracious Lord, Thine Arm Reveal
description: Now, Gracious Lord, Thine Arm Reveal in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 892 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “New Year. Prayer for a Blessing”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now, gra-cious Lord, thine arm re-veal, And make thy glo-ry known; Now let us all thy pre-sence feel, And soft-en hearts of stone.

lines: Now, gracious Lord, thine arm reveal,
Now let us all thy presence feel,
From all the guilt of former sin
And let the year we now begin,
Send down thy spirit from above,
That saints may love thee more,
And sinners now may learn to love,
And when before thee we appear,
And praise thee in our room.

licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
